V2 TVL is computed on-chain: (asset_1_reserves / 10^dec1) x price_1 + (asset_2_reserves / 10^dec2) x price_2, with prices from the §3.7 ladder and reserves from app 1002541853 local state. V1.1 TVL is the analytics API's reported liquidity_in_usd (§3.3, methodology_version 1.1.0).
Reserves are read on-chain (§5: 0.95) but the fact is denominated in USD, so §5's usd_conversion row governs: 0.90 x a TVL-weighted price confidence of 0.881 across the V2 pools.
Cross-check: across the 49 V2 pools whose analytics record was also read, our on-chain TVL differs from the source's own liquidity_in_usd by a mean 1.46%. A signal, never a value (§3.3).
last_day_volume_in_usd is reported in USD by the source; no conversion applied.

24h flows cover 70 of 70 included pools, 100.0% of included TVL. On-chain pool state has no 24h window, so V2 volume and fees come from per-pool analytics lookups while V2 TVL comes from on-chain reserves (§3.3): the two have different coverage, and this KPI describes the narrower one.
last_day_fees_in_usd is the TOTAL swap fee paid by users (LP + protocol) and is never reported as protocol_revenue (§3.3).

estimation_method: distinct transaction senders to Tinyman validator apps 552635992 and 1002541853 over rounds 64824112-64855612; that window is 31500 rounds at a measured 2.7436 s/round rather than an exact 24h boundary, because neither algod status nor the §1.2 indexer client exposes a block timestamp
notes: Counts ADDRESSES, not humans. One person with three wallets is three; a router batching for many users is one. No de-duplication is attempted, because any heuristic would be unfalsifiable (§4.1).
Interactions routed through an aggregator are attributed to the aggregator, not to the end user (§4.1).
Scanned 1551 application transactions; requested rounds 64824112-64855612, and the returned transactions actually spanned 64853616-64855609 (1993 rounds).
Confidence is capped at 0.80 for this KPI on every protocol: it is the least reliable metric published (§4.1).
